- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 2–5% upward bias to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply 1–3% upward adjustment for first 7 days.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags by 2–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change 1–2 days ahead.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >15% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise; use 5-day EWMA instead of 30-day forecast for smoothing.
